# Draft:Leibniz Research Centre for Working Environment and Human Factors

----
The Leibniz Research Centre for Working Environment and Human Factors (IfADo) is a non-university research institution based in Dortmund. It is concerned with the challenges of modern working environments. Its work focuses on research into basic life functions and processes, the assessment of health risks, and the performance- and health-promoting design and optimization of work tasks and work environments.
IfADo is a member of the Leibniz Association and an affiliated institute of the Technical University of Dortmund.
History
IfADo was founded in 1912 as ‘Kaiser-Wilhelm-Institute for Occupational Physiology’ in Berlin. In 1929, the institute was relocated to Dortmund where it was continued as Max-Planck-Institute (MPI) in 1948. In 1969, it was split up into two independent institutes, the MPI for Molecular Physiology and the Institute for Occupational Physiology (IfADo). Joint funding by Federal and stategovernments commenced in 1977.
In 2009, IfADo changed its name to Leibniz Research Centre for Working Environment and Human Factors. IfADo was last evaluated in 2024. An independent, international and technically relevant group of experts was appointed for the evaluation.
Activities and structure
The core topics of IfADo’s research are:
·       People working in technical environments
·       External and internal factors of wellbeing and performance
·       The challenges of an ageing workforce
·       From understanding toxic mechanisms to safe handling of chemicals in modern working environments
Since 2015, IfADo is structured into four scientific departments: (1) Toxicology, (2) Immunology, (3) Ergonomics, and (4) Psychology & Neurosciences.
